I5.quote: Series of Pt-loaded graphene oxide (GO)/HKUST-1 composites were synthesized by the reaction between Pt@GO and precursors of HKUST-1.

notes: I2 rests on PG, the Pt-loaded graphene oxide (Pt@GO), whose H2 uptake at 77 K is plotted in Fig. 6 (main p. 5, black circles to about 1.15 bar) and given as 0.2 wt% in Section 3.5. The paper gives Pt content of PG as 18.9 wt% by EDS (main p. 4, Section 3.3, Fig. S6), so the rest is GO, a schema material class (graphene_oxide); this is a metal-decorated carbon under protocol section 3. The paper does not give PG's C wt% itself; the Fig. S6 EDS spectrum shows C as the dominant peak. HPG0 is HKUST-1 (MOF), and HPG5/HPG10 are MOF-majority composites (EDS Pt 1.46 and 3.38 wt%), so these are not carbon sorbents; the carbon-sorbent status of the paper depends on PG alone. I4 is met on the literal wording (a surface area for at least one sample the paper reports measurements on): BET areas are given for HPG0, HPG5 and HPG10 (Table S2) but not for PG or GO (PG described only as 'significantly low and negligible porosity', Fig. 5). H2 uptake at 298 K and up to 80 bar is measured only on HPG0, HPG5 and HPG10 (Fig. 8), not on PG. I1: the 77 K and 298 K low-pressure isotherms were run on an ASAP 2020 (Micromeritics), a static volumetric analyzer, though the paper does not use the word volumetric; the gravimetric statement quoted covers I1 on its own. No retraction notice in the text, is_retracted is false, the paper is a primary research article, and it makes no statement that its H2 values were published before.
